question: Investigate the long-term behavior of the recursive map T(n): if n mod 3 == 0 then T(n) = n/3, if n mod 3 == 1 then T(n) = 4n+2, if n mod 3 == 2 then T(n) = 2n-1. Identify cycles, divergence patterns, invariants, and plausible conjectures.

   The system requires a few foundational conditions to be analyzed. One must define what it means for a number to be divisible by 3 (i.e., through modular arithmetic). The rules governing \( T(n) \) are contingent upon this divisibility. Therefore, an essential category is the classification of integers based on their equivalence classes modulo 3.

2. **Boundary Conditions (Schematism):**
   The boundary conditions involve partitioning the space of possible integers into distinct equivalence classes modulo 3: \( n \equiv 0 \pmod{3} \), \( n \equiv 1 \pmod{3} \), and \( n \equiv 2 \pmod{3} \
